sections.Af1:
-p-
Setup could not find a .HTML file association in the registry
-a-
It appears that you do not have a web browser installed.

NetStorm understands how to use a web browser to display links to web sites on the internet.
If you do not have a web browser installed, some of the links in the on-line help will not work.
However, these links are not critical to playing and enjoying the game.
-s-
Install a web browser.
sections.Af2:
-p-
Setup could not find the file associated with .HTML files in the registry.
-a-
It appears that you had a web browser installed at one time, but the program has been moved
or deleted.

NetStorm understands how to use a Web browser to display links to web sites on the internet.
If you do not have a Web browser installed, some of the links in the on-line help will not work.
However, these links are not critical to playing and enjoying the game.
-s-
Reinstall your web browser.
sections.Bf1:
-p-
Setup was unable to initialize the Windows Sockets system.
-a-
It appears that you do not have TCP/IP support installed on your computer.

NetStorm uses TCP/IP for all network communication.  Without TCP/IP the game will start, but you will be unable
to play online.
-s-
Install TCP/IP support from either the Windows install disks or CD, or from your ISP's install software.
If you have any question about this, consult your ISP's technical support.

[Bf2|Hf1|If[1,4,7]]
-p-
Setup detected an error while attempting to create a new socket.
-a-
Although you have TCP/IP support installed, it is not functioning properly.

NetStorm uses TCP/IP for all network communication.  Without TCP/IP the game will start, but you will be unable
to play online.
-s-
Reinstall Windows TCP/IP support or consult your ISP's technical support.

[Df[1-2]]
-p-
Setup did not detect DirectDraw or DirectSound on this machine.
-a-
It appears that you have not installed the latest version of Microsoft's DirectX.

DirectX did not ship with Windows 95, and has been through multiple revisions.
NetStorm requires the latest version of DirectX in order to run, and will install it
during the regular installation process.
-s-
If you get this during the initial diagnostics, complete the installation, reboot, and try
the diagnostics again. If it fails again, consult customer support.
sections.If5:
-p-
Setup could not connect to the diagnostic server.
-a-
Since you passed the ping tests, the most like reasons for this failure are:
* You are behind a firewall or proxy
* The diagnostic server is down.

Firewalls are used to make computers on a LAN fairly inaccesable to the Internet at large.
They do this by examining packet traffic between the LAN and the Internet, blocking traffic to or from
certain ports.

Proxys are similar, but instead of blocking traffic from the LAN machines to the Internet, they perform
operations on behalf of the LAN machines.  This is sometimes used to provide an entire LAN with internet access
via a single dialup account.

ISPs, in general, do not firewall or proxy their customers.
-s-
If you are dialing into an ISP with a single machine, then the problem is with the diagnostic server.  You will still
be able to run the game, and may even be able to play, since the diagnostic server is seperate from the game
server.

If you are on your company's LAN, the most likely problem is an outbound firewall. You should ask your LAN administrator to
open up the firewall for you on ports 6799 and 6800.

-a-

sections.Ef:
-p-
Less than two of the pinged addresses responded.
-a-
It appears that you are not connected to the Internet. This could be for a number of reasons:
* You are not dialed into your ISP
* You are unplugged from your network connection.
* You are connected or dialed in, but your ISP or LAN has lost its connection to the Internet.
-s-
Check all network connections (dial in if connected via modem), and re-run the diagnostics.

If the problem persists, check with your ISP or LAN administrator.
sections.Ff:
-p-
Less than two of the test sites could be looked up by name.
-a-
It appears that you are unable to perform DNS (Domain Name Service) lookups.  This could be for a number of reasons:
* DNS has not been enabled for your TCP/IP protocol.
* Your DNS server is down or your network connection to it is down.
-s-
Enable DNS for the TCP/IP protocol in your Network Control Panel.
If you have problems, consult your ISP or LAN administrator.
sections.Hf2:
-p-
Setup could not look up the address of the NetStorm's diagnostic server by name.
-a-
It appears that you are unable to perform DNS (Domain Name Service) lookups.  This could be for a number of reasons:
* DNS has not been enabled for your TCP/IP protocol.
* Your DNS server is down or your network connection to it is down.
-s-
Enable DNS for the TCP/IP protocol in your Network Control Panel.
If you have problems, consult your ISP or LAN administrator.
sections.If2:
-p-
Setup could not bind a socket to one of the diagnostic ports.
-a-
It appears that your are running another copy of Setup, or some other program is using the same ports that
NetStorm uses.

TCP/IP uses a 'port number' to route incoming packets to the appropriate program.  Each port number may be used by only
one program.  One of the port numbers used by NetStorm is already in use on your computer.  You will not be able to
go online until this port is freed.
-s-
Close all unneeded programs and try the diagnostics again.  If the problem persists, call customer support.

[Hf[4-7]|If([3,6-7,9]|1[0-3])]
-p-
Setup detected an uncommon socket error while running the diagnostics.
-a-
This indicates a problem with the TCP/IP protocol software.

You will still be able to run the game, but you may not be able to play online.
-s-
Try running the game and getting online.  If you can play online, then the error was probably transient.

If the error persists, or you cannot get online, contact customer support.
sections.Hf8:
-p-
At least one of the transmit tests passed, and at least one failed.
-a-
This may indicate that your connection to the Internet is firewalled on one of the ports used by NetStorm.
This could also happen if the NetStorm diagnostic server is experiencing problems.
-s-
Try running the game and getting online.  If you can connect to the server, you will be able to play, but you
will not be allowed to become the BattleMaster, who is the host of a battle.

If you cannot connect to the server, then you are either blocked on port 6800, or the NetStorm server is down.

Contact your ISP or LAN administrator to see if you are blocked on port 6800 outgoing and 6799 incoming and outging.
If you are not blocked on these ports and the problem persists, contact customer support.
sections.If14:
-p-
At least one of the recv tests passed, and at least one failed.
-a-
This may indicate that your connection to the Internet is firewalled on one of the ports used by NetStorm.
This could also happen if the NetStorm diagnostic server is experiencing problems.
-s-
Consult your ISP or LAN administrator to see if you are blocked on port 6799 incoming and outgoing.

If you are blocked incoming, you will still be able to play, but you will not be allowed to become the
BattleMaster, who is the host a battle.

If you are blocked outgoing, you will not be able to play.

If you are not blocked on this port and the problem persists, contact customer support.
sections.Ec:
-p-
The ping tests were cancelled before they completed

-a-
If you cancelled the ping tests because they appeared to be locked up, then you may not
be connected to the Internet.

-s-
Connect to the Internet via your normal means, and try again.  If the lockup persists,
contact your ISP or network administrator to verify that your Internet connection is
working properly.
sections.Fc:
-p-
The name lookup tests were cancelled before they completed.

-a-
If you cancelled the lookup tests because they appeared to be locked up, then you may not
have a network connection to your DNS server, or your DNS server may be down.

-s-
Confirm that you are properly connected to your ISP or LAN and try again.  If the lockup
persists, contact your ISP or network administrator to verify that your connection is
working properly and that the DNS server is up.
sections.Hc|Ic:
-p-
Some of the connection tests were cancelled before they completed.

-a-
If you cancelled the tests because they appeared to be locked up, then any of the following
problems may be the cause:
* You are not connected to the Internet
* You are behind a firewall or proxy
* You are connected to the Internet, but your ISP or LAN has lost its Internet connection.

-s-
Confirm that you are properly connection to your ISP or LAN and try again.  If the lockup
persists, contact your ISP or network administrator to verify that your connection is
working properly.

sections.DirectDrawManager:
{H2}Direct Draw

{Text}
This game uses Microsoft's "Direct Draw" technology to 
give you fast full-screen game performance. 
Most modern games use DirectDraw.  However,
for optimal performance NetStorm uses a few DirectDraw features
that many other games don't use, and which may or may not
work on all video cards.

Consequently, we have provided several options which let you tune
NetStorm to your particular video card.  As you toggle options,
it is possible that your machine will crash. If this
occurs, simply reboot and run NetStorm again. NetStorm will
return to the last known good mode.  But, to be safe,
you should close all other applications before selecting {CText}Start Direct Draw{Text} below.

{CText}For Windows Legacy users Hit ALT-ENTER any time to return to a window!{Text}

{CText}For Windows XP users, to go into windows mode simply press and hold CTRL-ALT-ENTER. For other operating systems use ALT-ENTER.{Text}

sections.AdjustDirectDraw:
{H2}Direct Draw

{Text}
You can often drastically improve the performance of NetStorm
by changing some of the options below.
Each option will be explained when you select it (before it is activated.)

Remember that if your video card does not support a particular
feature, some of these options may lock up your machine.  
It is recommended that you shut down all other
applications before changing these options.

As you change each feature, NetStorm will prompt you to
accept the change, and will automatically revert in 15 seconds
if you do not.

In case your machine crashes, restart and NetStorm will return
to the last known good mode.

{CText}If you can't see your mouse, try pressing F12!{Text}

{CText}Hit ALT-ENTER any time to return to a window!{Text}

sections.intro1082:
{H2}Netstorm Update v10.82

{CText}What's New?

{Text}This update brings multiple fixes, improvements and balance changes that breathe new life into Netstorm.

{CText}New Unit Added

~[ISunBattery.1]{Text}The Sun Generator is a cheaper, sun-only generator that aims to boost strategies involving Sun-only or rushing with a Sun Workshop.

{CText}Borderless Window

{Text}You now have the option to go fullscreen in window mode, allowing Netstorm better support for Windows 10.

{CText}Fairer Geysers

{Text}Geyser spawns in multiplayer are now balanced by default. They will generally spawn in pairs, one for each side.
sections.intro1082page2:
{H2}Netstorm Update v10.82 - Page 2

{CText}North / South Advantage - Fixed!

{Text}Previously certain units had advantage based on your starting location. This was caused by a bug which is now fixed. 
Ranges are adjusted based on direction so that they are equal regardless of the unit appearance.

{CText}Reworked Balance

{Text}The balance for the game was given a huge overhaul. While iconic units remain mostly the same, changes were made to nearly every other unit.
Air is much more powerful but so is anti-air. Golems are slightly slower to encourage teching into collectors, which are faster.
Most units will behave the same but Bulfs are now invulnerble to air and collect TWO storm crystals at a time.

{CText}Greater variety

{Text}Multiplayer maps are now capable of spawning in 16 million different variations. Additionally, there are new battlemaster options including the ability to change bridge sets (with new bridges!).
sections.intro1082page3:
{H2}Netstorm Update v10.82 - Page 3

{CText}Island Modification

{Text}It's now MUCH easier to move your residence or re-roll a new island. Just left-click on your fort in the Multiplayer menu and you'll see the new options.

{CText}Multiplayer Statistics

{Text}Your fort will now record every unit you build and many other fun statistics. You can view this by clicking your fort and selecting ~jView Stats~w.

{CText}Titles & Achievements

{Text}Unlock new titles in multiplayer battle to display below your name in the zones. The more you play, the greater your progress. Discover how close you are to unlocking the next title by selecting ~jChange Title~w from the Multiplayer Fort menu.

NetStorm!
"He who desires peace should prepare for war." -Anonymous

The goal in NetStorm is simple: Capture enemy Priests and Sacrifice them
to the Furies to gain secret Knowledge and Power.

NetStorm's controls are also simple:

Left-click to pick up and drop objects.

Right-click to get more options and information.

Scroll the screen by moving the mouse to a screen edge 
(in Full Screen and 640x480 resolution running in Window mode) or by
holding down the ALT key to scroll towards the cursor (in any mode).

The Escape key displays an options menu at the top of the screen.
Scrolling
For now, practice scrolling around your island. 
When you hit F4 to return to your island the tutorial will continue.

Hit F8 at any time to review the instructions.
Bridges
"Let the islands lean against the bridge,

And the bridges lean against the air."

--Book of Nimbus

To your left is the Production Window. You'll notice that it contains oddly
shaped bridge pieces. You can left-click one to pick it up. Move it over the 
world and then left-click again to drop it.

Bridges must attach to the edge of an island or to the open end of another bridge. 
If the bridge is completely red while you are dragging it then it
isn't attached or it might be blocked by something below it.

Note that you cannot connect bridges to an island where there is vegetation hanging over the edge.

Try dropping a few bridges.

REMEMBER: You can press F8 at any time to review the instructions.
Rotating Bridges
"If the shortest distance between two points is a straight line, 
we wouldn't build bridges like this, would we?" --Euclidius, 4th Century.

If a bridge isn't pointing the direction you would like, right-click to 
rotate it. Left-click as usual to put it into the world.

If you pick up a bridge you don't want, hit ESCAPE to return it to the
Production Window. You can also drop the bridge back into its place 
in the Production Window by left-clicking there.

One more thing: You can use the keys: q, w, a, and s
to quickly select bridges.
Bridge Quality
When a bridge appears in the Production Window, it is initially
cracked.  If it is left in the Production Window for a while, it
will become solid.  Cracked bridges
are weaker and tend to break.
Thus, if you build bridges too quickly, the quality of your work will be low and
you may pay the price later!

Bridges left hanging out over the sky,
unconnected to any island, will crumble from their own weight. Anything
standing on the bridge will fall!

This tutorial will continue once you've dropped a few more bridge pieces.
(Try right-clicking to rotate them!)
Storm Power, Part 1
"The coagulation of the Geyser into Crystal form is like watching white fire turn to ice."
--Freiken Drupe, Nimbian Naturalist

Above the Production Window is a number which shows your
Storm Power. Storm Power is required to build battle Units in Nimbus - it is the
essence of creation and destruction - and that means you want a lot of it!

Geysers contain Storm Crystals which can be harvested for Storm Power.

"Storm Geyser"       "Storm Crystal"
Storm Power, Part 2
Build a bridge from your island out 
to a Geyser. Don't worry if you have trouble connecting your bridge to the
Geyser - it just takes practice; and, if you wait long enough a misplaced bridge
will crumble anyway.

Notice that if you've put a bridge in the proper place to connect with an island, a small
extension will appear on the end of the bridge to close the gap.  Use this to help
you figure out when you are connected to the Geyser.

Hint: Press F2 to make all the tall objects transparent so you can see through them.
Press F2 again to return it back to normal.

The tutorial will continue once you have connected to a Geyser.

"Storm Geyser"
Harvesting Storm Power
Now that you have attached to a Geyser,
you can begin to harvest the Storm Crystals that it produces.

Left-click on your Priest and then left-click 
on the Geyser. Your Priest will begin to walk to the Geyser and
will return as soon as he has retrieved a Storm Crystal.

Hint: F5 will center the screen on your Priest.

This tutorial will continue once your Priest returns to the Temple with a 
Storm Crystal.

     "Priest"
The Temple
The Priest is going to the Storm Geyser to gather Storm Crystals. Each time he
returns to the Temple he delivers another Crystal.

The Temple has the
magical ability to turn Crystals into Storm Power - you'll see the number
above the Production Window increase.

Let the Priest continue gathering until you have 600 Storm Power. In the meantime,
practice building bridges to other Geysers.
Mission Accomplished!
Congratulations, you have completed the first Tutorial.

The next Tutorial will describe how to create weapons of war.
sections.NoBridgeYet: Just practice scrolling now. Hit F4 to go home when you're ready to learn about bridges.

Buildings, Part 1
"Priests just chant a bunch of nonsense, and suddenly there's a big, 
perfect building.  No wonder people want to kill them."  --Nikro Huvaks, Unemployed Nimbian Carpenter

Your Priest has the ability to transform Storm Power into several special
kinds of buildings: Temples, Workshops, and Altars.
Buildings, Part 2
The Temple transforms Storm Crystals into Storm Power and produces bridges.

The Workshop makes battle units.

                "Temple"                         "Workshop"
Create a Temple
You have been given sufficient Storm Power to create a Temple.
Right-click on 
your Priest and select Construct and then choose Temple and then Build Wind Temple.

The cursor will become a Wind Temple. You may lay it any place your Priest can
walk. Red areas will indicate where it overlaps things. You
will only be able to drop it when there are no red areas remaining.

Once you've placed it in a legal area, your Priest will walk to the build location and begin construction.

Try it now!  (Use F8 if you need to see these instructions again.)
Temple Complete
You may have noticed that as soon as the Temple was complete, the color
of the edge of the island changed.  This is because the 
owner of this temple (in this case, you) now controls this island.
Once you control an island, you can build other units
on that island and build bridge pieces off of it as well.

(F7 toggles the ownership colors on and off.  If you didn't
see the color change, you may have this display turned off.)
Create a Workshop
Now that you have created a Temple, use the Priest to create a 
Workshop.

Just like you did for the Temple, right-click on 
your Priest and select Construct and then choose Workshop and Build Sun Workshop.

The cursor will become a Sun Workshop. You may lay it any where your
Priest can walk. Red areas will indicate where the Workshop overlaps things. You
will only be able to drop it when there are no red areas remaining.

Try it now!
Production
"The Nimbian aptitude for complex mechanics is simply unsurpassed." --Desil Prottus, Nimbian Mechanic.

Workshops can build weapons.
You start off with the Knowledge of only a single weapon: The "Sun Disc Thrower."
This machine hurls miniature suns at your enemies.  You will gain the
Knowledge of other weapons as you capture Priests in battle and
sacrifice them to the Furies!  But for now, you will just have to make do!

To start producing the Sun Disc Thrower, right-click on the 
Sun Workshop and select Put Knowledge Into Production.  At the top of the menu
you'll see that there are two production slots 
available.  Fill a slot by selecting "Sun Disc Thrower."
First Weapon, Part 1
"Sun Disc Throwers decapitate the clumsy." -Major Tomas Rultoff.

Your Production Window now contains a round device - the Sun Disc Thrower.
You can place it in the world by left-clicking on it and then
left-clicking again to drop it (just like bridges).

Notice that it turns red where you can't drop it, just like everything else.
First Weapon, Part 2
Placing weapons has one more constraint, called Energy. When you pick up
the Sun Disc Thrower you'll see a little icon next to it. A lit icon 
means the unit is receiving the Energy required to build it. 
A gray icon  means that it isn't.

Drop a single Sun Disc Thrower now and we'll explain more in a moment.

Take note of where you could and couldn't build the Sun Disc Thrower.
Weapon Displays
While you were dragging the Sun Disc Thrower you probably noticed that 
there was a ring encircling it.  This ring shows the range of the
weapon.  You can display this range at any time by left-clicking
on a weapon that is already built in the world.

Try that now, and then build another Sun Disc Thrower near the
first one.  Try to maximize the target area covered by the two Sun Disc Throwers.
Energy, Part 1
"There is not a single law of nature that Energy cannot flaunt and break."
--Jan Kilterstern, Nimbian Energy Specialist.

As we mentioned before, all weapons require a certain amount
of Energy in order to be constructed.  There are three flavors of
Energy: Wind , Rain  and Thunder .

Some weapons, like the Sun Disc Thrower, can use any kind
of Energy.  A requirement of any Energy is called: "Sun" 
since it lacks domination from any of the three Storm Furies.

For example, something that requires Wind Energy  must be supplied
with one Wind Energy in order to be built.  However, something that requires one
Sun Energy can be supplied with Wind, Rain or Thunder.
Energy, Part 2
The Wind Temple that you have built on your island generates
Wind Energy in a circle around it.  You can left-click
to see the range.

Click on it now to see the range.

The tutorial will continue a few seconds after you have displayed the Energy range
of the Temple.
Energy, Part 3
Now that you know that the Wind Temple is providing Energy
around it, you can see where it is legal to build a Sun Disc 
Thrower and where it is illegal.  The Sun Disc Thrower 
requires one unit of any Energy and the Wind Temple
generates two units of Wind Energy.

Build a few more Sun Disc Throwers.  Try to build a bridge away from
the island and build a Sun Disc Thrower at the end of the bridge.
Notice that if you are too far away, the  icon on the left
of the cursor will turn to a .

You can only build units at the ends of bridges, not
just anywhere along the edges!

The tutorial will continue when you have built two more Sun Disc Throwers.
Energy, Part 4
One last word about Energy.

Energy is only required to construct a weapon, 
not to run it.  Once any Unit has been built,
it will continue to operate until it is destroyed by the enemy
or salvaged by you.  It does not consume Energy or Storm
Power after it is built.
Salvaging
After a unit has been built, you may salvage it to recover a fraction
of its value.

Try it now. Right-click on one of the Sun Disc Throwers
you just made and choose Salvage.  The amount of Storm Power
that you will receive is inversely proportional to the damage
that the Unit has received up to that point.

The tutorial will continue when you have salvaged anything.
Mission Accomplished!
Congratulations, you have completed Tutorial Two.

The next Tutorial introduces battles!

Capture The Priest!
"There is no greater serenity than that which follows the sound cudgeling of an enemy."
--Gen. Ebens Rilfenstor

Now that you know how to build Workshops and assign 
Production you can use the weapons that these
Workshops produce to attack the enemy!

In order to speed things along, there is already a Wind Temple
and Sun Workshop built for you.  Normally you would need
to build these yourself.

Notice in the production window on the left
that you now have the ability to create Golems.  Golems are special
servants of the Temple and can be used to harvest 
Storm Power.
Build Golems
You can create Golems like you did the Sun Disc Thrower. They require
one Sun Energy  (i.e. one Rain, Wind, or Thunder).

You'll need more Storm Power this time. Build a bridge out
to a Geyser, then build several Golems and have 
them begin to harvest Storm Power from that Geyser.  
Notice that the Golems are much more efficient at gathering Storm Crystals than
Priests are.

The tutorial will continue when one of your Golems
has returned to the Temple with its first Storm Crystal.
Capturing Enemy Priests, Part 1
"The only difference between a captive Priest and a dead one
is a little time."  --Belkis Reveskis, Nimbian warlord.

South of your island is the enemy's island. Your goal is to
capture the enemy Priest.

Priests are immortal on the battlefield.  However,
when they get shot they become incapacitated and may be
taken hostage.  You can then bring them back to your island
and Sacrifice them to the Furies in order to gain more Knowledge.
Capturing Enemy Priests, Part 2
Build bridges from your island and attach to the
enemy island. 

Bridges are free, so if you have a hard time connecting
to the enemy island at one place, try branching off and connecting at 
another location.

Hint: Don't worry about building cracked bridges for the time being,
there won't be many explosions to cause them to fall.  Just
practice building the bridge as fast as you can for now.

The tutorial will continue when you have connected
to the other island.
Build Sun Disc Throwers
Excellent! Now that you have connected to the enemy island,
you can begin the assault.  Begin by putting Sun Disc Throwers into
production.

Right-click on the Sun Workshop as you have done before and 
choose Put Knowledge into Production.  Then select
Sun Disc Thrower.
Generators, Part 1
"With a hundred of these, you can fuel the future." --Berlis Smirtenk, Inventor of the 
Generator

You are going to use the fire power of the Sun Disc Throwers
to attack the enemy Priest.  Your goal is to drop them
on the enemy island to begin the pursuit!

When you try to drop a Sun Disc Thrower on the enemy island
you will find that nowhere on that island does the Energy
from your Temple reach far enough.  You need to
extend your Energy using a device called a "Generator".
Generators, Part 2
There are three kinds of Generators just as there are three
kinds of Energy: Rain, Wind, and Thunder.  There is no
"Sun" Generator because "Sun" is a universal energy 
that can be fulfilled by Rain, Wind, or Thunder.

Each Generator produces one unit of its flavor of Energy
in a circle around it just as the Temple does.

The tutorial will continue when you have added "Wind Generator" 
to the production of your Workshop.

   "Rain Generator"         "Wind Generator"         "Thunder Generator"
Extending Energy, Part 1
As mentioned, a Generator radiates Energy in a circle surrounding it.

Notice that the Generator itself requires one unit of Sun (i.e. any) Energy.
Thus, you must build your first Generator near the Temple.  Then, 
you can build another Generator using the Energy cast from the first.
In this fashion, you can extend your Energy wherever you need it.
Extending Energy, Part 2
Right now, you need Energy on the other island so that you can build
Sun Disc Throwers there.  Build a series of Wind Generators starting
from your island extending across the bridge until you have
extended the Energy all the way to the enemy island.

The tutorial will continue when you have built your first 
Sun Disc Thrower on the enemy island.

Remember: You can only build weapons off of the ends of bridges or on
an island; you may not build off the side of a bridge.

Hint: You may need to build more bridges off of the ones you already have
in order to get the Generators where you need them.
Incapacitating the Enemy Priest
"You know you have them cornered when they become utterly
motionless except for the eyes, which dart about, wild with panic."
--Prut Nilduk, referring to Priests on the battlefield.

When the enemy Priest is within range of your Sun Disc Throwers
they will automatically begin to shoot at the Priest.
If the Priest is not within range, build more Sun Disc Throwers until
he can not escape.  You may need to extend your Energy across
more of the enemy island in order to build more Sun Disc Throwers.

The tutorial will continue when the Priest has been incapacitated from
the damage you inflict.
Capturing the Enemy Priest
Now that the priest is immobile (you can see the protection field surrounding him),
you can use a Golem to go capture him.  
Left-click on the Golem and order him to move to
the vicinity of the Priest.

Notice that when you are choosing the
destination of the Golem the mouse cursor will change to a hand shape when
it is directly over the priest.

If you left-click when the cursor is a hand icon
then you are ordering the Golem to walk there and capture the Priest.
You can only capture the Priest when the Priest has been immobilized.

The Golem can only carry one thing at a time.  If you don't see the
hand cursor, it may be because your Golem already 
has his hands full with a Storm Crystal. Order him to drop it first by 
right clicking on him and choosing Drop Storm Crystal.

The tutorial will continue when your Golem has captured the Priest.
Mission Accomplished!
You have captured the Priest!  Normally, you would now
Sacrifice him to the Furies, but
we'll wait until the next tutorial to introduce that.

That completes Tutorial Three.
The next tutorial will describe how to use Sun Disc Throwers and Sun Cannons
to decimate your enemies and how to Sacrifice for new Knowledge.

Advanced Combat, Part 1
"Those who advance blindly find trouble.  Victory always lurks in the corners."
--General Dalik Marridelt

As always, your goal is to capture the enemy Priest.
However, you will notice that now the enemy island is defended
by Sun Cannons and Sun Disc Throwers.

"Sun Cannon"

The Sun Cannons have a long range, but they have a serious
limitation: they can only fire in straight lines North, 
South, East and West.  You will learn how to destroy
these Cannons with your Sun Disc Throwers despite the superior range
of the Cannon.
Advanced Combat, Part 2
Begin as you have before by collecting Storm Power with Golems.
There is already a Wind Temple and a Sun Workshop built for you,
but you still need to put the Sun Disc Thrower and the Wind Generator into production.

The tutorial will continue when you have both of these in production.
Sun Disc Thrower vs. Sun Cannon, Part 1
You need to destroy the enemy's Sun Cannons before you have
a hope of capturing the Priest.

If you were to naively attack a Sun Cannon head-on with a 
Sun Disc Thrower, the superior range and fire power of the Sun Cannon would 
destroy the Disc Thrower long before it had a chance to 
inflict much damage.

However, since Cannons can only shoot in straight lines, a Sun Disc Thrower
can safely attack it from a diagonal angle.
Sun Disc Thrower vs. Sun Cannon, Part 2
Build bridges towards the Sun Cannons and situate them so that
you have bridge spurs in a location diagonal to each Cannon.  Don't get too
close to the edge of the island though, you want to stay out
of range of the Sun Disc Throwers to the South.

Remember, you may have to build Wind Generators 
to extend your Energy as you have done before.

Hint: You can left-click on Cannons and Disc Throwers to see their attack range.

The tutorial will continue when you have destroyed the Cannons.
Upgrading Workshops, Part 1
There are six Sun Disc Throwers on the enemy island.
You could attempt to overwhelm these
Disc Throwers with Disc Throwers of your own, but it is not very
efficient.  Instead, you can build your own Sun Cannons and destroy the Disc Throwers
from outside of their range.

Multiplayer islands begin with the Sun Disc Thrower and the
Sun Cannon in your Knowledge base.
Upgrading Workshops, Part 2
You should add Sun Cannon to the production of your Workshop now.
However, you will find that you do not have enough production slots
in your Workshop to put Sun Cannons into production.
You will need to "Upgrade" your Workshop first in order to
gain another production slot.

Right-click on your Workshop and select Upgrade.
You may have to gather more Storm Power in order to afford
the upgrade.

The tutorial will continue when you have put Sun Cannons
into production in your newly upgraded Workshop.
Sun Cannons vs. Sun Disc Throwers
Build Sun Cannons outside the range of the enemy Sun Disc Throwers
directly in line with them from the North, South, East, or West.

Cannons do have a little flexibility - you don't have to
align them perfectly with their target.  As long as the gun barrel of
your cannon is lined up with base of the target, it should be able hit it, assuming it's within range.

One more thing: You may notice that during combat you gain Storm Power
each time you destroy an enemy Unit.  Indeed, you can often gain more Storm
Power by destroying the enemy than you can through harvesting.

The tutorial will continue when you have destroyed the enemy Disc Throwers.

Hint: You might toggle Options / Cursor Snap To Grid and see if that
helps you lay things down more easily.
Enemy Sun Disc Throwers Destroyed
"Too often a drowning man pulls down his would-be saviors."
--Anonymous

You may have found that it was easier to destroy the Sun Disc
Throwers than you expected.  This is because as one exploded, it
threw shrapnel which damaged the others.

Shooting units always explode in this way, and chain reactions can
wipe out closely packed groups.

Be sure to take this into consideration before you attack or build
a dense pack of shooting weapons.
Sacrificing Priests, Part 1
Go capture the Priest as you have done before using a Golem.  When you have done
so, you can bring him back to your island and sacrifice him
to the Furies to learn new knowledge.

Incidentally, normally you can use any Transport to capture an
enemy Priest.  You'll use a Golem for this example.

One more thing: a carrier such as a Golem cannot carry more than one
thing at a time.  When you left-click on the Golem, the object he is
carrying will flash briefly.  In order to pick up the Enemy Priest, you will
need to drop any Storm Crystals that the Golem might be carrying.  Right-click
on the Golem and Choose "Drop".

The tutorial will continue when you have captured the enemy Priest with a Golem.
Sacrificing Priests, Part 2
Sacrificing the enemy Priest to the Furies allows you to gain new knowledge.
To begin the sacrificial process, you must build an Altar.  Right-click
on your Priest (not the one you just captured) and order him to
Build Altar.

You might not have enough room on your island to build an Altar.  If this is the case,
you can "Salvage" a Workshop to get more space.  Right-click on the Workshop
and choose "Salvage".

The tutorial will continue when you have built the Altar.
Sacrificing Priests, Part 3
Now that you have an Altar built, you need to bring the enemy Priest 
to the center of it.  Order the Golem that is carrying the enemy Priest
to go to the center of the Altar.  He will tie the enemy Priest up and
walk away once he arrives there.

The tutorial will continue when the enemy Priest is bound to the Altar.
Sacrificing Priests, Part 4
Now that the enemy Priest is bound to the Altar, you need to 
order your Priest to begin the ritual which will 
ultimately grant you new Knowledge.  Left-click
on your Priest then left-click on the Altar when the
cursor has changed to a knife.

Your Priest will walk
to the Temple and begin the ritual.  He will build five runes.
When all of them are complete, the Altar will collapse and the Sacrifice will be complete!

The tutorial will continue when the ritual is complete.
Multiplayer vs. Single Player
There is a slight difference between sacrificing a Priest in
the Multiplayer Arena vs. in the single player missions.

In the single-player missions, a Technology profile is granted to 
you as part of the challenge of the mission, thus you do not gain Knowledge 
by Sacrificing in a mission.  The sacrifice is instead usually considered the "win."

When playing in the Multiplayer Arena, on the other hand, the Knowledge that you play with
survives from one battle to another.  Thus, when you Sacrifice a Priest
in a Multiplayer battle, you will be given a choice of which Knowledge
you wish to gain.
Mission Accomplished!
That completes Tutorial Four.

The next tutorial will describe how to use
defensive Units to defeat weapons much more powerful than your own.

Defense, Part 1
"A Strategy is not enhanced by numbers." -- Tzu, Sun Warrior

This time, you are overwhelmed by superior fire-power.

The enemy island has "Thunder Cannons" which have incredible range
and damage.  The enemy also has "Whirligig Bases" which can 
send flying Whirligigs to attack you from above!

  Thunder Cannon                   Whirligig Base
Defense, Part 2
Meanwhile, you are already under attack!

The Thunder Cannon off the southern island is already attacking
your Temple.  You need to interpose a defensive piece quickly in order to stop
this attack.

You have knowledge of a technology called the "Stone Tower."  This piece 
can absorb a lot of damage before disintegrating and can thus 
be used as cover for other units.

Put "Stone Tower" into production in the Workshop that is already built on your island.
Then build a Stone Tower directly in the line of fire of the Cannon.  You have
no time to waste!

The tutorial will resume when the Stone Tower is under fire.
Building Additional Workshops
Excellent, now that you have stopped the attack on your Temple, you
have a few moments to prepare a counter-attack.  The Stone Tower
will not last forever, but when it collapses you can replace it with another one.

Meanwhile, you need to put "Sun Disc Thrower," "Sun Cannon," and "Wind Generator"
into Production, but you only have one slot left in your Workshop.
The last time you ran out of slots in a Workshop, you Upgraded to
increase its capacity. Another way to increase the number of available production slots
is to build an additional Workshop.

There's room to the South-West of your Temple for another Workshop.

The tutorial will continue when you have put "Sun Disc Thrower," "Sun Cannon," and "Wind Generator"
into production.
The Enemy Island
"If you ask why the Temple protects its island, it will immediately fail to do so."
--Book of Nimbus

In previous tutorials, the enemy island did not have a Temple on it.
A Temple has the power to protect its island from enemy intrusion by
disallowing the enemy to build pieces there.  In this tutorial, however, there
is a Temple on the enemy island.  So, you will have to build 
all of your weapons on bridges for this mission.

Notice that the center Thunder Cannon is too far from the edge of the island
to be attacked by Sun Disc Throwers.  You will need to attack it with a Cannon of your own,
but this is going to require some defenses.
Defending Against Aerial Attacks
"The only way to make the Mud-gig more irritating would be to give it wings."
--Gril Hegberk, two years before flight was perfected.

The enemy also has a "Whirligig Base" which can launch flyers
to attack your units.  Whirligigs are very powerful because they can
easily move from one target to another.  However, they have two weaknesses which you can exploit.

First of all, they are vulnerable to Disc Throwers since 
Disc Throwers can shoot at them while they move.  Secondly, the Whirligigs
must return to their bases periodically to refuel which increases their 
exposure to gun fire.  Also, if their base is destroyed, they run out of fuel and die.

During this attack, as you advance on the enemy island, you will need to use your
Sun Disc Throwers to provide cover for your Cannons and Stone Towers from the aerial Whirligigs.

Go inspect the enemy island now and left-click on the Whirligig Base. The tutorial will
continue a few seconds after you have selected the Whirligig Base.
Defending Against A Cannon, Part 1
"Stone Towers are built from the outside in . . . 
within every third layer of bricks is the body of a brave man."
--Unknown

If you use a Stone Tower as a shield as you did earlier, you can draw the fire from
the Thunder Cannon and build Sun Cannons behind the Tower and shoot
the Thunder Cannon.

Build a bridge towards the Thunder Cannon.  Build a Stone Tower close
to the enemy island and in the line of fire.  Then build Sun Cannons
behind the Stone Tower.

There's a trick to this - you can build bridges off of the
small island that is under a unit that you build.  So, you can
build the Stone Tower first, then add a short bridge segment behind it,
then you can build a Sun Cannon off of that bridge.  Repeat this and you can have a whole
line of Cannons all attacking the same place!
Bridge Quality
When you build bridges now, the quality matters.  
When one of your pieces is destroyed the shock will cause adjacent cracked bridges to collapse.  
This will make your attack much more difficult.  Try to build un-cracked bridges this time; 
use cracked ones only as a last resort.

Bridge is not targeted by guns.  However, it can be destoryed.  
Generators have the ability to "meltdown" causing collateral 
damage to objects and bridge nearby.  Thus, if you find that you need to clear
bridge (yours or the enemies) use the Meltdown! option
of a Generator. (Multiplayer Only)

The tutorial will continue when you have destroyed the Thunder Cannon
and the Whirligig Base on the enemy island.  This is a hard one, good luck!
Spells
"For their own safety, encourage your children never to read strange Obelisks."
--Ancient Parental Proverb

Notice that on the enemy island there are several obelisks.  These are 
ancient artifacts which hold the instructions for magical spells.
When one of your Golems reads the runes on the obelisk, it is able to
cast that spell.  Many of these spells are very useful.

Order a Golem to walk to the obelisk.  Look for the cursor to 
change to a "hand" icon and then left-click.

The tutorial will continue when you have granted a spell
to any Golem.

 "Obelisk"
Devastation Spell
You have found a "Devastation Spell".  Order the Golem to
move near the enemy Priest.  Then right-click on the 
Golem and order him to Cast Devastation.
That should get the Priest's attention!

Notice that when you left-click on the Golem,
you see the radius of the spell as well as an icon telling
you which spell this Golem has.

Use the spell to help you capture the enemy Priest and ultimately
Sacrifice him.
Sacrificing the Priest
A quick review on Sacrificing the enemy Priest:

1. Have your Priest build an Altar.

2. Carry the captured enemy Priest to the center of the Altar.

3. Order your Priest to begin the ritual. Order him to
walk to the Altar by left-clicking on your Priest then left-click
on the Altar when the cursor changes to a knife.

4. Wait while the Priest performs the ritual. (In a real game, you would
need to be on the lookout for the enemy trying to get the stolen Priest back!)

The tutorial will continue when you have Sacrificed the enemy Priest.
Mission Accomplished
That completes Tutorial Five.

The next Tutorial introduces Aerial Transports and the advantages of using
Wind, Rain and Thunder aligned units.
sections.VortexDestroyed:
Temple Destroyed!
Your Temple has been destroyed.  You can
not process Storm Power or build bridges now which will make the mission very difficult to
complete.  Next time, be sure to keep an eye on the Stone Tower that is
meant to protect the Temple.  If you want to start the Mission again, press ESC, and select
Restart Mission from the Game menu.
sections.FactoryDestroyed:
Workshop Destroyed!
Your Workshop was destroyed.  You can not build some of your units
now.  If you have enough Storm Power, you can build another to replace the previous one.
If not, either gather more or restart the mission.

Themed Units
"What sins have we committed to deserve such power?"
--Captain Villus Spakesmere, referring to a bloody victory

This time, you'll face a new class of defensive piece. But you'll have more 
advanced weaponry at your disposal as well.

The world of Nimbus is ruled by three Furies: Wind, Rain, and Thunder. So far
all your pieces have been aligned with none of these and are thus referred to as "Sun."
Sun units are flexible and easy to use, but not as specialized or powerful as the aligned units.
Air Ships
In this tutorial you will use pieces aligned with the Wind Fury. First you'll
use the "Air Ship." This unit is a heavily armored Aerial Transport, able to 
deliver Storm Crystals, acquire Spells, and capture enemy Priests while withstanding considerable 
hostile fire.

You don't have Golems for this Mission.  Use the Air Ship to harvest Storm Power instead.
Because it flies, you don't have to build bridges to the geysers now!

            "Air Ship"
Aligned Energy, Part 1
In addition to their high Storm Power costs, advanced units like the Air Ship
have more formidable Energy requirements.

As discussed before, Energy is aligned with Wind, Rain, or Thunder. 
The Air Ship, for example, requires two Wind Energies and one of any kind (i.e. "Sun").
When you are constructing the Air Ship, the cursor will display
two wind icons  and one sun .  
As you move the cursor, the icons will light up when you have met 
the requirements at a given construction site.  Each Generator and Temple can only
supply one unit of Energy at a time.  Thus, since the Air Ship requires two
Wind and one Sun, you must have at least three supplies
of Energy; for example, two Wind Generators and a Rain Temple would satisfy the
Energy requirements of an Air Ship.

These are the Energy icons:

Unlit:                                                     

Lit:                                                         

            "Wind"      "Rain"        "Thunder"         "Sun"
Aligned Energy, Part 2
Remember that your Wind Temple generates one unit of Wind Energy around it.  Thus, in order
to build an Air Ship, you will need to build two Wind Generators in order to
satisfy the Air Ship's construction requirements.

One more thing: A Sun Workshop can not build aligned units.  In order to build an Air Ship,
you will need to construct a Wind Workshop.

Build a Wind Workshop now with your Priest.  Enable production of the "Wind Generator" and
the "Air Ship."  The tutorial will continue when you have built an Air Ship.
Aerial Transports
"Sure they're faster. Sure they're easier. But for my money, 
there's still nothing compares to good-old Bridge."
--Jameson Hoofa, Founder, Bridge Builder's Union

The interface for commanding Aerial Transports is similar to the one for moving
Golems and Priests (which are Ground Transports). To send your Air Ship out for 
Storm Crystals, left-click on it and then left-click again on the destination Geyser.

The tutorial will continue when you've used your Air Ship to bring a Storm Crystal
back to your Temple.

Hint: Be careful of those guns to the South!
Crossbows, Part 1
For this tutorial, we have given you knowledge of the Wind aligned unit "Crossbow."
The Crossbow has a much longer range and more powerful kick than a Sun Disc Thrower.

However, it cannot fire in all directions.  Instead, it has a limited arc from the direction it is
constructed. 

Put the Crossbow into production now.  You'll have to upgrade your Wind Workshop first.

The tutorial will continue when you have enabled production of the Crossbow.

"Crossbow"
Crossbows, Part 2
"When they pay us more, maybe we'll make them swivel all the way around."
--Anonymous Crossbow Archer

When you construct a Crossbow, you can right-click to change which quadrant
it can fire in.  The range display will show you what can be hit.

Lay down a Crossbow now on your island to defend against any attacks from the Whirligigs.
Practice rotating it before you drop it.
The Crossbow requires one Wind Energy and one Sun Energy. It also
costs {global.crossbowCost} Storm Power, so you'll need to make sure your Air Ship keeps
retrieving Storm Crystals as you fight.

The tutorial will continue when you have built one Crossbow.
Barricades
"Between Nimbus and the Beyond stands an infinite, burning barrier." -Book of Nimbus.

Your opponent in this mission has erected a Sun Barricade on his island. 
Four posts are generating a protection field which blocks all gun-fire
between their endpoints. You can't succeed until you destroy 
the Barricades.

Surprisingly, the Crossbow alone is enough to defeat the enemy's island.  
Be sure to stay out of the direct line of fire of the
Thunder Cannons since you do not have a blocker to use as a shield!

The tutorial will complete when you have destroyed all of the enemy
Thunder Cannons, Whirlibases, and Sun Disc Throwers.
Do not worry about capturing the Priest for this battle.  Good luck!

    "Sun Barricade"
Mission Accomplished

"An uneducated man is harmless.
A well-educated man is unbeatable.
A half-educated man is merely dangerous."
--Anonymous

Good work! This completes the tutorial. Consider yourself half-educated.  
To complete your education, you'll have to pit your new skills against NetStorm's many
single-player missions.

The world of Nimbus contains over twenty unique units 
you can use in battle, each with its own strategic advantages. 
You will learn about each of them as you continue with the Campaign missions.
Remember to right-click and select About to view information
about each new unit as you encounter it.

You can continue with the Campaigns or play online now.

Have fun!
